Detailed explanation of why OpenAI's "0.1%" data is untenable

Official statement: "the vast majority of usage has shifted to GPT‑5.2, with only 0.1% of users still choosing GPT‑4o each day."

They used "users" (total users), not "paying users" or "Plus/Pro users".

They emphasise this occurred "after we restored access during GPT-5 release" (i.e. after August 2025 when paid users regained 4o access) and "learned more about day-to-day usage".

However, the baseline is total users: ChatGPT's weekly active users had already exceeded 700-800 million at that time (2025 data frequently cited 700-800M WAU), with monthly figures even higher.

What was the actual proportion of paying users? According to reliable 2025-2026 data, paid subscribers (Plus + Pro + other consumer-tier paid tiers) roughly ranged between 10-35 million.

ChatGPT Plus/Pro paying users numbered approximately 10-20 million (The Information, DemandSage, etc. estimated 10-35 million). Additionally, ChatGPT Pro ($200/month premium tier) accounts for 5.8% of consumer sales, though its total volume remains small.

Overall paid penetration rate: approximately 5% (The Information reports 5% for 2025, targeting 8.5% by 2030; other sources indicate similar figures, with free users constituting the overwhelming majority).

Thus, among 700-800 million total users, the paying cohort tops out at tens of millions (5% = approx. 35-40 million upper limit, likely lower in practice).

Now applying this 0.1% to the paying cohort:

If 0.1% represents 0.1% of total users → Daily active 4o selectors ≈ 700-800k (0.001 × 700-800 million) .

However, free users will be entirely barred from using 4o from August 2025 onwards, meaning these 700,000–800,000 users are exclusively from the paying base (only Plus/Pro subscribers retain access to 4o).

Assuming a total paying user base of 20–35 million → the actual daily proportion selecting 4o is 2–4% (potentially higher if the paying base is smaller).

This represents a remarkably loyal niche cohort—individuals willing to pay an extra $20 monthly to retain 4o's "warmth," "less stringent safety filtering," and "creative flair."

Yet OpenAI frames this as "only 0.1% of users," using the total user base (predominantly free) as the denominator to imply "low adoption."

Compounding this is routing behaviour:

Even when paying users select GPT-4o, sensitive/emotional/creative/edgy prompts are frequently routed by the safety system to GPT-5.2. Usage from these rerouted instances isn't counted in "choosing GPT-4o" statistics—further depressing the figures.

Result:

The actual proportion of paying users genuinely wanting GPT-4o far exceeds the "0.1%" figure, but this data undergoes multiple layers of "optimisation" to become the company's shield.

The total number of paying users is already small (less than 5% of all users), and 4o has been locked within Plus/Pro since August 2025. The 0.1% figure is calculated using the total user base (which includes vast numbers of free users).

This equates to packaging "2-4% of paying loyal users who remain staunchly committed to 4o" as "0.1% of all users", making it sound like "virtually no one uses it".

Among the 5% paying users, 2-4% utilise 4o – half of them, in fact. And this 0.1% figure is manufactured through triple filtering: manipulating the denominator, siphoning usage via routing, and imposing paywalls? Not many? How is this not significant?

OpenAI is perpetrating statistical fraud and psychological manipulation.
Stop pretending. Can we have some honesty?
